findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite the ordering rationale: pipeline goes first because `idempotent_reuse` would replay an agentic attestation. Require `force=True` on any pipeline re-run after the agentic run, and treat a run with `verdict_replayed: true` as invalid evidence.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:544-547: `idempotent_reuse` runs under the pipeline engine whenever sign and not force
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:120-199: `idempotent_reuse` checks only `claim_gate_check`, never the engine, and returns `runner: "reused"`, `model: None`, `coverage.llm_ran=False`
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:185-187: `gate_status` exposes this case only through `verdict_replayed`
findings.finding: The plan's reason for running pipeline first is wrong. Agentic runs skip every shortcut regardless of order, so 'the agentic run is not shortened by a reuse shortcut' protects against nothing. The real hazard is the reverse: `reuse.idempotent_reuse` never checks the engine. If an agentic PASS has signed a current attestation, a later pipeline run without `force` returns the replayed agentic attestation (`runner: "reused"`, `model: None`, `coverage.llm_ran: False`). It runs no pipeline review. The order is correct, but the plan does not cover this hazard: re-running the pipeline after the agentic run (for example after an INDETERMINATE) would be silently replaced by the replay.
findings.location: Approach → Runs ("The pipeline run goes first so the agentic run is not shortened by a reuse shortcut")
scenarios: The pipeline run ends INDETERMINATE (for example, a Bedrock spend-cap deny), the agentic run PASSes and signs, and the operator re-runs the pipeline. It returns a replayed PASS with no LLM call, and that replay gets recorded as the production pipeline result.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: "The pipeline run goes first because the pipeline's idempotent-reuse shortcut does not check the engine and would replay a signed agentic PASS. Any pipeline re-run after the agentic run uses `force=True`, and a run whose `gate_status` shows `verdict_replayed: true` does not count."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the ordering rationale: pipeline goes first so the PIPELINE run is not short-circuited by idempotent_reuse replaying an agentic-signed attestation (reuse.py does not check the engine).
evidence: Plan: "The pipeline run goes first so the agentic run is not shortened by a reuse shortcut: shortcuts are pipeline-only and stay off under `agentic`."
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:544: `if engine == "pipeline" and sign and not force and not retry: reused = reuse.idempotent_reuse(...)`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:139-141: idempotent_reuse checks only claim_gate_check(...).ok, with no engine check, so an agentic-signed certified attestation would satisfy it.
findings.finding: The plan's reason for running pipeline first is backwards. The agentic run can never be shortened by a reuse shortcut: all three shortcuts are gated on engine == 'pipeline'. The real risk is the other way round. idempotent_reuse does not check which engine signed the attestation, so if agentic ran first and PASSed, the later pipeline run would return a reused PASS (llm_ran=False, runner='reused') without running the pipeline. The order is right, but the stated reason would lead an executor or a later reader to think the order does not matter for the pipeline run.
findings.location: Approach → Runs: "The pipeline run goes first so the agentic run is not shortened by a reuse shortcut"
scenarios: An executor reasons that the agentic run is immune to shortcuts either way, swaps the order or re-runs the pipeline after the agentic run, and records a reused PASS as the pipeline's production run.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: "The pipeline run goes first: the reuse shortcuts are pipeline-only, and idempotent_reuse accepts any certified attestation regardless of engine, so a pipeline run after an agentic PASS would replay it instead of reviewing."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a read-only precondition that the production Bedrock spend-cap deny is not in effect (or that the window has reset) before starting the runs, and state that a run ending INDETERMINATE for an environmental reason is re-run after the cause is cleared.
evidence: Epic comment 2026-11-12 06:30 PST: "production Bedrock is denied by BedrockDailySpendCapDeny, which is attached to rebar-gerrit-instance-role ... stops ... any production review for lobo. It lifts at 00:00 UTC (16:00 PST)."

findings.finding: Production Bedrock availability is not a precondition. The epic records that BedrockDailySpendCapDeny is attached to the production instance roles and blocks every production review until 00:00 UTC. A run started while the deny is in effect fails on provider access. The plan's only failure handling is "record INDETERMINATE and investigate", which spends the run and does not lead to the AC's "completes".
scenarios: The executor starts both runs during the cap window. Both end INDETERMINATE on access denial, and the evidence shows the cap, not the engines.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a pass condition: the agentic run's `coverage.engine` == "agentic" and `plan_review_status.engine` == "agentic"; the pipeline run's engine is absent or "pipeline".
evidence: "the engine (`coverage.engine`, absent = pipeline)"
AC lists "engines" only as a recorded field, with no expected value
findings.finding: The AC records the engine but never asserts that the recorded engine matches the requested engine. A deployed server that ignored engine="agentic" and fell back to pipeline would still satisfy the AC as written.
scenarios: The engine argument is dropped by the MCP surface. Both runs execute the pipeline, both record a verdict, and the AC is ticked.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the AC: 'and for each run the recorded `coverage.engine` (and `plan_review_status.engine` after the run) equals the requested engine (absent or "pipeline" for the pipeline run, "agentic" for the agentic run); a mismatch fails the AC.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <deployed sha>` for the merge commit of each of the six children (or of the latest-merged one), not just surfaces.
evidence: "The engine children have landed: switch ..., agentic arm ..., adapter ..., attestation engine ..., surfaces ... and harness ..."
"`git merge-base --is-ancestor <surfaces commit> <deployed sha>` true"
findings.finding: The deploy precondition lists six child tickets but checks ancestry for only the surfaces commit. Unless surfaces is guaranteed to have merged last, the check does not prove that the adapter, attestation engine or harness commits are deployed.
scenarios: Harness or the attestation engine merges after surfaces. The deployed SHA contains surfaces but not the later child, yet the precondition passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single check with: for each child merge commit C in {switch, agentic arm, adapter, attestation engine, surfaces, harness}: `git merge-base --is-ancestor C <deployed sha>` must exit 0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a default maximum wait (e.g. 30 minutes per run) after which the job is recorded as non-terminal/hung with its last gate_status and investigated like INDETERMINATE.
evidence: "poll `gate_status(job_id)` until terminal"
findings.finding: Polling 'until terminal' has no bound, so there is no wait limit and no rule for a job that never reaches a terminal state.
scenarios: An agentic run stalls on a Bedrock call. The executor polls indefinitely or picks an arbitrary cutoff.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Poll gate_status every ~30s for at most N minutes; if not terminal by then, record the last gate_status as a hung run and treat it as INDETERMINATE.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the AC's recorded-field list match the Recorded section, including terminal gate_status, post-run plan_review_status verdict/engine, and resolution_class when INDETERMINATE.

AC: "The job ids, verdicts, engines, models, attestation status, deployed SHA and PST completion timestamps are recorded"
findings.finding: The Recorded section lists terminal gate_status, plan_review_status verdict/engine after each run, and resolution_class for INDETERMINATE runs. The AC omits all of these, so the AC is weaker than the described deliverable.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 1 vs Approach — Recorded
scenarios: The epic comment omits plan_review_status, so the change in persisted review state is never evidenced, yet the AC is ticked.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the is-ancestor check against the merge commit of every listed child (or the latest of them), not only surfaces, and record which commits were verified.
evidence: 'The engine children have landed: switch ..., agentic arm ..., adapter ..., attestation engine ..., surfaces ... and harness ...'
'must name a commit with git merge-base --is-ancestor <surfaces commit> <deployed sha> true'
findings.finding: The deployment precondition checks only that the surfaces commit is an ancestor of the deployed SHA. The plan lists six child tickets as prerequisites. If any of the other five (e.g. the harness or attestation-engine commit) merged after surfaces, this check passes even when that commit is not deployed.
scenarios: The harness or attestation-engine child merges to main after surfaces; the deployed SHA contains surfaces but not that commit; both runs exercise stale code and are recorded as production verification of the new engine.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single check with: for each child's merge commit C, require `git merge-base --is-ancestor C <deployed sha>` to be true, and list the C values alongside the deployed SHA in the epic comment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make each run provably a fresh LLM review: confirm `plan_review_status` reads `unsigned` before the pipeline run (or pass `force=True`), and record and require `coverage.llm_ran` true and `runner` ≠ `reused` for each run.
evidence: reuse.py:168-190: a reused verdict carries coverage {llm_ran: False, idempotent_skip: True}, runner 'reused', model None, sidecar_emitted False.
reuse.py:202-232: verdict_reuse replays a stored pipeline BLOCK with zero LLM calls.
Epic comment 2026-11-12 06:30: "Filed: mindless-misogynic-nematode (3359 advisories; also lobo's target ticket)", so other sessions can touch this ticket.
_mcp_llm.py:296-298: `force=True` creates a fresh job and is passed into _review_plan_body, which bypasses the reuse shortcuts.
findings.finding: Nothing checks that each run actually called the LLM rather than taking a shortcut. The plan relies on the ticket "never [having] been plan-reviewed", but it does not re-check this at execution time, does not pass force=True, and does not record coverage.llm_ran / coverage.idempotent_skip / coverage.verdict_reuse / runner. If another session reviews the ticket first (it is already named as another ticket's target), the pipeline run returns a reused verdict with model=None and runner='reused'. That would be recorded as a completed production run.
findings.location: Approach → Runs / Recorded; Acceptance Criteria line 1
scenarios: Someone reviews mindless-misogynic-nematode with the pipeline engine before this ticket runs. The production pipeline run replays that PASS or BLOCK without calling Bedrock, and the comment records it as evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the pipeline run, check that `plan_review_status(ticket)` returns verdict `unsigned` and that no REVIEW_RESULT sidecar exists; otherwise pass `force=True`. Add `coverage.llm_ran` and `runner` to the per-run Recorded fields, and treat a run with llm_ran=false as not completed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Write the deployed-SHA read as two steps: `aws ssm send-command --profile frontier --instance-ids i-00880b2c7f13527c5 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters 'commands=["cat /var/lib/rebar/mcp-deployed-sha"]'`, then `aws ssm get-command-invocation --profile frontier --command-id <id> --instance-id i-00880b2c7f13527c5`. Read StandardOutputContent once Status is Success, following infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md.
evidence: Plan: "an SSM `cat /var/lib/rebar/mcp-deployed-sha` on the host (`aws ssm send-command --profile frontier`) must name a commit with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <surfaces commit> <deployed sha>` true"
Repo prior art: infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md:79 — "Then `aws ssm get-command-invocation --profile frontier --command-id <id> --instance-id <instance-id>`."
AWS CLI reference: get-command-invocation's StandardOutputContent holds the first 24,000 characters of stdout and stays empty until ExecutionStatus is Succeeded or Failed.
AC provenance names the host i-00880b2c7f13527c5, but the precondition command has no --instance-ids or --document-name.
findings.finding: The precondition says the deployed SHA is read by 'an SSM `cat /var/lib/rebar/mcp-deployed-sha` on the host (`aws ssm send-command --profile frontier`)'. That assumes send-command returns the command's stdout, and it does not. send-command only starts the command asynchronously and returns a CommandId. The file contents come from a separate `aws ssm get-command-invocation --command-id <id> --instance-id <id>` call, which returns them in StandardOutputContent after the command finishes. The repo's runbook already uses this two-step pattern. The command shown also leaves out the target instance and the document (`--instance-ids i-00880b2c7f13527c5 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript`), even though the AC names that instance.
scenarios: The operator runs only `aws ssm send-command` and gets back a CommandId but no SHA, so the ancestry check has nothing to compare against.
The operator calls get-command-invocation before the command finishes and gets an empty StandardOutputContent, which could be taken as 'marker missing'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the precondition's parenthetical with: "(`aws ssm send-command --profile frontier --instance-ids i-00880b2c7f13527c5 --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters 'commands=[\"cat /var/lib/rebar/mcp-deployed-sha\"]'`, then read the SHA from `aws ssm get-command-invocation --profile frontier --command-id <CommandId> --instance-id i-00880b2c7f13527c5 --query StandardOutputContent --output text` once Status is Success, as in infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md)".
